scope: Held-g R1/R5 anatomy, L4 lean replies and the held-g probe, as ported onto claude/alpha-next (the held-g twelve-arm queue and its leaves are not part of this build); hub CPU tests; no box or GPU evidence

leaves.name: anatomy-timing-event
leaves.replaces: torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) on the real lane composition
leaves.equivalence: As that module's docstring: record stamps a shared fake clock, so a device time is the fake clock at the moment the command's event was recorded; elapsed_time is the stamp difference in ms; synchronize returns at once and logs the lane state; the spans' host clock is the same fake clock (one CLOCK_MONOTONIC domain). The credit harness leaves are native41_fixture_leaves.json's, unchanged. Declared here because that test names this file.

leaves.name: lean-reply-format-selection
leaves.replaces: NativeSegmentDriver._open_replies: the arm's native_progress 'replies' selection and the auto-arm ownership check
leaves.equivalence: The r4 stack has no NativeProgress and no auto-arm policy; _open_replies returns the format under test, the only value the real method returns. Everything after it is production code: OpenRequest.replies, the worker bridges' lean build/send, the driver's _ingest_lean, LeanStream, the journal, the census and the release streams. The real selection (control reply, status, auto-arm ownership, every chunk opened lean) runs in e3_native41_held_g_probe's -lean modes on the connected Core.
leaves.cannot_prove: The control-plane path to the selection; that is the held-g probe's.

leaves.name: lean-completion-order
leaves.replaces: real device-event completion timing on four ranks
leaves.equivalence: r4's ControllableEvent completes only when the test sets it; a seeded subset completes per driver tick (all in finalize), so completions land out of op order and pending sets are non-empty. Full and lean runs see the same order because the event creation order and tick structure are identical (asserted: same envelope and reply sequences). Every other r4 leaf is r4's own, declared in test_e3_r4_worker_bridge's docstring.
leaves.cannot_prove: Real completion timing, PP channel timing or GPU work.

leaves.name: held-g-probe-rpc-counter
leaves.equivalence: The probe's execute and sample fixtures do not go through collective_rpc, so the 'rpcs' column is zero by construction there; the counter it reads is the one collective_rpc increments, proven in test_e3_native_reply_hol.
leaves.cannot_prove: Stock RPC counts on the box.

leaves.name: held-g-probe-idle-wait-landed
leaves.equivalence: DirectTransport computes every reply synchronously at submit, so a reply has always landed when the owner waits; the leaf records the call and returns True. The real wait (landed, timeout, closing, failed) is test_e3_native_anatomy.IdleWaitTransport over the real ReplyTransport.
leaves.cannot_prove: Reply latency or the wait's timeout on the box.

leaves.name: held-g-probe-idle-predicate-flips
leaves.replaces: one stock input a step would carry, per flip
leaves.equivalence: Each flip adds one sentinel to the real scheduler/manager/encoder-cache container (or one queued batch entry, or an abort queue the CPU engine leaf lacks), checks the real predicate, removes it and checks again, before the step goes on.
leaves.cannot_prove: That the box scheduler never holds another pending input kind; the predicate's names are pinned against the vllm source in test_e3_native_anatomy.IdleSourceNames.

leaves.name: held-g-probe-lean-revalidation
leaves.equivalence: The observer returns the production object unchanged and also builds WorkerCompletionReport(**fields) with its validating constructor, counting a mismatch; it changes no state.

leaves.name: anatomy-fake-clock-and-spans-emit
leaves.equivalence: DeviceSpans and StepAnatomy take the clock and the emit callable as parameters; the fake clock advances by a fixed step per read and emit appends the text, so every sum and class is exact and checkable.
